newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Late profit-taking chokes off Taiwan stock surge.
newsitem.headline: Late profit-taking chokes off Taiwan stock surge.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Thursday as profit-taking swept the market in late trade, snapping a weeklong winning streak, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 23.97 points or 0.36 percent lower at 6,629.68.
Turnover was a heavy T$64.97 billion.
Prices opened higher and seemed poised to further a recent bull run during which the index gained nearly 300 points.
But the momentum died after the market-leading financial and electronics sectors rose to levels that made profit-taking irresistable for many investors, triggering the late downturn.

"The market was hoping for financials and electronics to continue leading the way, but the two sectors have already risen so much that profit-taking was inevitable," said Wang Jieh, analyst for Foremost Investment.
Electronics, bullish for weeks on sound earning reports, lost 0.67 percent with Taiwan Liton dropping T$1.10 to T$47 and United Microelectronics falling by T$0.50 to T$37.20.
The heavily weighted financials fell 0.48 percent as Hua Nan, one of the "big three" state-run commercial banks, closed T$1 lower at T$125.
Brokers said bullishness in some markets from Wall Street's overnight record high -- widely seen as approval of President Bill Clinton's re-election -- did not impress Taiwan investors.
"I don't think too many investors really considered Wall Street's rise and the U.S. election as big factors," Foremost's Wang said.
Brokers expected Taiwan's market to settle into a short-term consolidation before mounting a new challenge to the 1996 closing high of 6,653.65 that was set on Wednesday.
A 6,580-6,640 range was seen for Friday.
